bull.b: The substantially complete How Mine expansion should increase processing capacity and support a higher production base once commissioning and ramp-up are completed. Entering 2027 at an annualized rate above 30,000 ounces could improve operating scale and strengthen the company’s core asset base.

Bringing Redwing back into production adds a second operating growth avenue and uses existing underground infrastructure and processing plants. The restart is planned without relying on the feasibility study outcome, while internally generated funding limits the need for initial equity issuance.

Stronger operating cash generation provides internal funding for expansion and restart activities, reducing reliance on external capital for near-term development. Although cash was reinvested into the business, the improvement indicates that operations are generating more support for growth initiatives.

bear.b: Persistently negative equity is a major structural weakness because it reduces financial flexibility and leaves the company more vulnerable if operating performance deteriorates. Even with relatively low absolute debt, the capital structure provides a limited cushion for absorbing setbacks or funding future investment.

The large working capital deficit creates ongoing pressure to convert gold production into cash and maintain access to funding. Near-term borrowings and purchase commitments further constrain flexibility, making execution of expansion and restart programs more dependent on reliable operating cash flows.

Reduced production guidance and higher expected all-in sustaining costs weaken the economics of the current operating plan. Lower ounces spread fixed costs across a smaller production base, while elevated costs can limit cash generation and make the company more sensitive to operational execution.
